title: Right to Be Forgotten Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to exercise your right to be forgotten and delete personal data from online services. Protect your privacy with data erasure.
intro: This comprehensive checklist helps you exercise your right to be forgotten by systematically removing personal data from online platforms and services. Follow these steps to reduce your digital footprint and protect your privacy.

items.task: Create a secure email account for data requests
items.why: Protects your main email from potential data breaches and keeps deletion requests organized in one place.
items.howTo: Set up a new email account using a privacy-focused provider like ProtonMail. Use this exclusively for data deletion requests and document all communications.

items.task: Document all online accounts and services
items.why: Creates a comprehensive list of platforms that may have your personal data, ensuring nothing is missed in the deletion process.
items.howTo: Check your main email for account creation confirmations, review browser saved passwords, and use tools like Incognito Browser to search for forgotten accounts.

items.task: Identify data brokers with your information
items.why: Data brokers collect and sell personal information without direct consent, making them critical targets for deletion requests.
items.howTo: Search major data brokers like Whitepages, Spokeo, and BeenVerified for your name, phone, and address. Document findings for removal requests.

items.why: Facebook collects extensive personal data and tracks users across the web, making deletion crucial for privacy protection.
items.howTo: Go to Settings > Your Facebook Information > Delete Your Account. For GDPR users, use the specific data deletion request form citing Article 17.

items.task: Delete Google account data and services
items.why: Google maintains detailed profiles including search history, location data, and behavioral patterns across all their services.
items.howTo: Visit myaccount.google.com, go to Data & Privacy, and either delete specific services or your entire account. Download data backup first if needed.

items.why: Professional networks contain sensitive career and contact information that can be used for targeted attacks or unwanted solicitation.
items.howTo: Go to Settings & Privacy > Account preferences > Closing your account. For partial deletion, use Privacy settings to limit data sharing first.

sections.title: Data Brokers and Background Check Sites

items.task: Submit opt-out requests to major data brokers
items.why: Data brokers sell personal information to marketers, employers, and potentially malicious actors without your direct consent.
items.howTo: Visit opt-out pages for Acxiom, LexisNexis, Epsilon, and other major brokers. Each has different procedures - some require phone calls or mail requests.

items.task: Remove listings from people search engines
items.why: These sites aggregate public records and social media data, creating detailed profiles accessible to anyone with internet access.
items.howTo: Submit removal requests to Spokeo, WhitePages, BeenVerified, and PeopleFinder. Use Incognito Browser to check if removals were successful after 30 days.

items.why: Background check services maintain detailed personal records that can affect employment and housing opportunities if inaccurate or outdated.
items.howTo: Send written requests to major companies like HireRight, Sterling, and Checkr requesting deletion of personal data under applicable privacy laws.

items.why: Many companies ignore or delay deletion requests, requiring persistent follow-up to ensure compliance with privacy laws.
items.howTo: Create a spreadsheet tracking request dates, company responses, and follow-up deadlines. GDPR requires responses within 30 days maximum.

items.task: Monitor for re-appearance of deleted data
items.why: Some services may restore data from backups or continue collecting information even after deletion requests are processed.
items.howTo: Set monthly reminders to search for your information on previously contacted sites. Use different browsers including Incognito Browser for unbiased results.

items.why: Companies that refuse to delete data may face regulatory penalties, and documentation supports potential legal remedies.
items.howTo: Save all email communications, screenshots of data still present, and response letters. Contact data protection authorities if companies remain non-compliant.
